title: [YouPass Collect] - North American Household Composition in 1970-2003
prompt: The table below shows the household composition in a North American country from 1970 and 2003. Summarize information and make comparison where relevant

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table compares the percentages of various household types in a North American country in 1970 and 2003.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while most household categories experienced growth during this period, married couples saw a significant decline. In addition, married couples remained the most common household type in both years, despite the substantial decrease.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding family households, married couples accounted for the majority in 1970 at 61%, far exceeding other member sharing households at 13%, which in turn was slightly higher than mother with children at 10% and father with children at 9%. By 2003, the proportion of married couples had dropped considerably to 41%, representing a decline of 20 percentage points. In contrast, the remaining three family household types all increased marginally by approximately 1%, with other member sharing households reaching 14%, mother with children rising to 11%, and father with children climbing to 10% at the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for non-family households, which were relatively uncommon in 1970, single-person households stood at just 4%, slightly higher than room-sharing arrangements at 3%. Over the following three decades, both categories experienced substantial growth, with single-person households more than tripling to 13% by 2003, representing an increase of 9 percentage points. Similarly, room-sharing households increased nearly fourfold, accounting for 11% at the end of the period, which was an 8 percentage point rise from the initial figure.
